# Design Document

## Overview

`tighter-reviews` extends the `review-task prepare` flow and the per-runner config surface in `spec-workflow-mcp` along three independent tracks that share two integration points (`handlePrepare` in `src/tools/review-task.ts`, settings reads in `src/multi-server.ts`):

- **Track A — Typecheck pre-computation**: `handlePrepare` runs `tsc --noEmit` once and surfaces tagged diagnostics + coverage in the response, instead of asking the reviewer to hunt for type errors.
- **Track B — Diff-first context**: `handlePrepare` returns a `git diff -U10 -M HEAD --` of the in-scope files, so the reviewer reads changed hunks instead of full files. A new shared **path denylist** filters secrets/locks/binaries from both diff and hygiene paths.
- **Track C — Per-runner model selection**: a new `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)` helper resolves a grouped `adversarial: { model } / taskReview: { model }` shape with a legacy fallback. A small in-process settings cache (`mtime + size`-keyed) keeps repeated reads cheap.

The new `data` fields (`diff`, `diffStats`, `skippedPaths`, `diffTruncated`, `typecheckResults`) are additive; `filesToReview`, `hygieneSignals`, `methodology`, `taskContext`, `implementationSummary`, `steeringExcerpt` keep their current shape.

`buildReviewMethodology` grows new directives (R4.1, R4.2, R4.4–R4.7) that compose with the existing item-9 hygiene directive. Composite output is pinned axis-by-axis against fixture files (R4.10).

## Steering Document Alignment

### Technical Standards (tech.md)

There is no `tech.md` steering doc in this repo today. Defaults applied:
- TypeScript ESM, Node `child_process` (`execFile`) for shelling out — matches existing `src/core/git-utils.ts` style.
- Vitest with co-located `__tests__/` directories — matches `src/core/__tests__/hygiene-signals.test.ts`.
- No new runtime dependencies; `tsc` invoked via `node_modules/.bin/tsc`, never imported as a library.

### Project Structure (structure.md)

There is no `structure.md` steering doc. Conventions inferred from the tree:
- Pure async utilities live in `src/core/`. New modules (`task-diff.ts`, `typecheck.ts`, `path-denylist.ts`, `adversarial-settings.ts`) follow that pattern.
- Tool handlers live in `src/tools/`. `handlePrepare` stays the only orchestrator; the new utilities are called from it, not from `src/dashboard/`.
- Test fixtures: introduce `src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/` (new — no `__fixtures__` directory exists today; this is the first).

## Code Reuse Analysis

### Existing Components to Leverage

- **`computeHygieneSignals`** (`src/core/hygiene-signals.ts:45`) — extended to consume the new `pathDenylist` filter before scanning. Its public signature is unchanged; the denylist is applied internally.
- **`PathUtils`** (`src/core/path-utils.ts`) — used as-is for `getWorkflowRoot`. No additions.
- **`AdversarialRunner.run` / `TaskReviewRunner.run`** (`src/dashboard/adversarial-runner.ts:63`, `src/dashboard/task-review-runner.ts:58`) — already accept `model?: string` and forward it as `--model`. No signature change. Track C only changes which value is passed.
- **`handlePrepare`** (`src/tools/review-task.ts:118`) — gains a `Promise.all` shell after `allFiles` is computed (line 180). Track A lands the shell; Track B slots the diff utility into the existing seam.
- **`buildReviewMethodology`** (`src/tools/review-task.ts:360`) — gains new arguments (see Components and Interfaces) and emits new directives composed with the existing item-9 hygiene directive (line 422–426).

### Integration Points

- **`multi-server.ts` settings-read callsites**: lines 780–791 (adversarial initial), 948–959 (adversarial retry), 1730–1742 (task-review initial), 1774–1786 (task-review retry). All four sites switch to `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)`. The retry paths intentionally call the same resolver (R3.9).
- **`adversarial-settings.json` schema**: extended to optionally include `adversarial: { model }`, `taskReview: { model }`, and `features: { typecheck }`. Legacy top-level `model`, `cli`, `cliArgs` continue to work indefinitely.
- **MCP response schema**: permissive (`additionalProperties` allowed). New optional fields ship without a version bump.

## Architecture

`handlePrepare` orchestrates three pre-computation utilities concurrently. Each utility owns its external-process invocation, denylist application, and unavailable/timeout fallbacks. None throw out of `handlePrepare` — failures degrade to documented absent-with-reason states.

```mermaid
graph TD
    HP[handlePrepare] --> AF[allFiles from impl log]
    AF --> POOL[Promise.all]
    POOL --> DIFF[computeTaskDiff]
    POOL --> TC[runProjectTypecheck]
    POOL --> HYG[computeHygieneSignals]
    DIFF --> DL1[pathDenylist.filter]
    HYG --> DL1
    DIFF --> GIT1[git diff -U10 -M HEAD --]
    DIFF --> GIT2[git diff --numstat HEAD --]
    TC --> TSC[tsc --noEmit -p . --listFiles]
    POOL --> BM[buildReviewMethodology]
    BM --> FIX[fixture-pinned composite output]

    MS[multi-server.ts callsites] --> RRM[resolveRunnerModel]
    RRM --> CACHE[settings cache mtime+size]
    RRM --> AR[AdversarialRunner.run]
    RRM --> TR[TaskReviewRunner.run]
```

### Modular Design Principles

- **Single File Responsibility**: each new utility owns one concern (diff, typecheck, denylist, settings resolution).
- **Component Isolation**: `handlePrepare` is the only orchestrator; utilities don't call each other except through the shared `pathDenylist` module.
- **Service Layer Separation**: process spawning lives inside utilities; `handlePrepare` and `multi-server.ts` never call `execFile` or `spawn` directly for these concerns.
- **Utility Modularity**: denylist match logic is one module consumed by two callers (diff, hygiene), guaranteeing identical behavior.

## Components and Interfaces

### `src/core/path-denylist.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** decide whether an absolute path is denylisted from review surfaces (diff, hygiene).
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type DenylistDecision = { denylisted: boolean; reason?: string };
  export function isDenylisted(absPath: string): DenylistDecision;
  export function partitionPaths(paths: string[]): { kept: string[]; skipped: string[] };
  export const TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS: readonly string[];
  ```
- **Match semantics:** exact basename (case-folded), basename suffix, basename prefix, path-segment match. NOT glob; NOT git pathspec wildcards (R1.5).
- **Test-fixture exception:** if any path segment matches `TEST_FIXTURE_SEGMENTS` (`__tests__`, `__fixtures__`, `fixtures`, `test-data`, `testdata`, case-insensitive), the path is kept (R1.6).
- **Dependencies:** `node:path` only.
- **Reuses:** none.

### `src/core/task-diff.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** produce a unified diff and numstat of in-scope working-tree changes vs. `HEAD`, with truncation and binary-section stripping.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type TaskDiffResult = {
    diff: string;
    stats: { filesChanged: number; linesAdded: number; linesRemoved: number } | undefined;
    skippedPaths: string[];
    truncated: boolean;
  };
  export async function computeTaskDiff(
    projectPath: string,
    allFiles: string[]
  ): Promise<TaskDiffResult>;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  1. `partitionPaths(allFiles)` → kept + skipped.
  2. Run `git diff -U10 -M HEAD --` and `git diff --numstat HEAD --` concurrently with `cwd: projectPath`, `env: { ...process.env, GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS: '0' }`, kept paths as pathspec.
  3. Strip `Binary files ... differ` sections from the unified diff body.
  4. Apply per-file (500 added+removed lines) and total (50,000 byte) truncation; replace truncated file sections with `<diff truncated: <file> exceeded per-file/total cap>`. Set `truncated: true`.
  5. On any failure (not a git repo, `git` missing, non-zero exit) return `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths, truncated: false }`. Never throws.
- **Dependencies:** `node:child_process` (`execFile`), `path-denylist`.
- **Reuses:** `path-denylist`.

### `src/core/typecheck.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** run `tsc --noEmit` once per `handlePrepare`, return tagged diagnostics + coverage in the discriminated union shape from R2.2.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type TypecheckDiagnostic = {
    file: string; line: number; column: number;
    code: string; message: string; inScope: boolean;
  };
  export type TypecheckResult =
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'success';
        diagnostics: TypecheckDiagnostic[];
        coverage: { compiled: string[]; excluded: string[] };
        truncated?: boolean }
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'unavailable';
        reason: 'no-tsconfig' | 'project-references' | 'wrapper-config'
              | 'tsc-not-found' | 'no-parseable-output' | 'feature-disabled' }
    | { tsconfigPath: string; status: 'timeout' };
  export async function runProjectTypecheck(
    projectPath: string,
    allFiles: string[],
    opts: { enabled: boolean }
  ): Promise<TypecheckResult[]>;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  1. If `opts.enabled === false` → return `[{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'feature-disabled', tsconfigPath: <root>/tsconfig.json }]`.
  2. Resolve `tsconfig.json` at project root. If missing, has top-level `references`, or is `files: []` with no `include` → return `'no-tsconfig'` / `'project-references'` / `'wrapper-config'` accordingly.
  3. Resolve `tsc` from `<projectPath>/node_modules/.bin/tsc`. If absent → `'tsc-not-found'`.
  4. Spawn `tsc --noEmit -p <projectPath> --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile <projectPath>/.spec-workflow/.cache/tsc.tsbuildinfo --listFiles --pretty false` with `env: { ...process.env, FORCE_COLOR: '0', NO_COLOR: '1' }` and a 30 s timeout (SIGTERM → 2 s grace → SIGKILL).
  5. On timeout → `{ status: 'timeout' }`.
  6. Parse diagnostics and `--listFiles` output. If non-zero exit and zero diagnostics parse → `'no-parseable-output'`. If clean exit and zero `--listFiles` lines → `'no-parseable-output'` (R2.9).
  7. Compute `coverage.compiled = allFiles ∩ listFilesOutput`, `coverage.excluded = allFiles \ listFilesOutput`. Both sides normalized via `fs.realpathSync.native` + lowercase on case-insensitive volumes (R2.4). The reported arrays use the **original `allFiles` paths**.
  8. Tag each diagnostic with `inScope: file ∈ normalizedAllFiles`.
  9. Cap diagnostics at 100 (in-scope first, then out-of-scope), set `truncated: true` if capped.
- **Dependencies:** `node:child_process`, `node:fs`, `node:path`.
- **Reuses:** none. `path-denylist` is **not** applied to typecheck — tsc decides what to compile via `tsconfig`.

### `src/core/adversarial-settings.ts` (new)

- **Purpose:** parse `.spec-workflow/adversarial-settings.json` once per `(path, mtime, size)` and resolve per-runner model precedence.
- **Interfaces:**
  ```ts
  export type RunnerKey = 'adversarial' | 'taskReview';
  export type AdversarialSettings = {
    adversarial?: { model?: string } | null;
    taskReview?: { model?: string } | null;
    features?: { typecheck?: boolean } | null;
    model?: string;
    cli?: string;
    cliArgs?: string[];
  };
  export function loadSettings(projectPath: string): AdversarialSettings;
  export function resolveRunnerModel(
    settings: AdversarialSettings,
    runner: RunnerKey
  ): string | undefined;
  export function isTypecheckEnabled(settings: AdversarialSettings): boolean;
  ```
- **Behavior:**
  - **`loadSettings`**: in-process cache keyed by `(absPath, mtime, size)`. Both `mtime` and `size` must match the stored entry to use the cache (R3.7 — covers second-resolution mtime filesystems). Malformed JSON or top-level non-object → return `{}` and log a warning **once per process per file path**, with the warning flag cleared if and only if `(mtime, size)` advances.
  - **`resolveRunnerModel`**:
    1. If `settings[runner]` is an object with a non-empty string `model` → return it.
    2. Otherwise if top-level `settings.model` is a non-empty string → return it.
    3. Otherwise → `undefined`.
    4. `null`, missing, empty-string, non-object `settings[runner]`, non-string `model` are all treated as absent (R3.5–R3.6). Non-object `settings[runner]` logs a malformed-load warning.
  - **`isTypecheckEnabled`**: returns `true` unless `settings.features?.typecheck === false`. Anything else (missing, null, empty string, non-boolean) → `true` (R3.12).
- **Dependencies:** `node:fs`, `node:path`.
- **Reuses:** none.

### `src/core/hygiene-signals.ts` (modified)

- **Change:** before scanning, filter `files` through `path-denylist`. Files in `partitionPaths(files).skipped` are not scanned.
- **Public signature unchanged** (`computeHygieneSignals(files: string[]): Promise<HygieneSignal[]>`).
- **Skipped paths are NOT surfaced from the hygiene path** (they're surfaced from diff via `data.skippedPaths`). This avoids double-reporting the same skip.

### `src/tools/review-task.ts` — `handlePrepare` (modified)

- Inserts a `Promise.all` after `allFiles` is computed (review-task.ts:180):
  ```ts
  const settings = loadSettings(projectPath);
  const [diffResult, typecheckResults, hygieneSignals] = await Promise.all([
    computeTaskDiff(projectPath, allFiles),
    runProjectTypecheck(projectPath, allFiles, { enabled: isTypecheckEnabled(settings) }),
    computeHygieneSignals(allFiles),
  ]);
  ```
- Adds new fields to `data`:
  ```ts
  data: {
    /* existing */
    taskContext, implementationSummary, steeringExcerpt,
    filesToReview: allFiles,
    hygieneSignals,
    methodology,
    /* new */
    diff: diffResult.diff,
    diffStats: diffResult.stats,
    skippedPaths: diffResult.skippedPaths,
    diffTruncated: diffResult.truncated,
    typecheckResults,
  }
  ```
- **Track A landing**: only `typecheckResults` is added; `Promise.all` is in place but with `computeHygieneSignals` and a `Promise.resolve(emptyDiff)` placeholder. **Track B landing**: replaces the placeholder with `computeTaskDiff` and adds the diff fields.

### `src/tools/review-task.ts` — `buildReviewMethodology` (modified)

- New signature:
  ```ts
  function buildReviewMethodology(
    taskContext: { /* unchanged */ },
    hasTechSteering: boolean,
    hasPriorReviews: boolean,
    hasHygieneSignals: boolean,
    diffState: 'present' | 'present-truncated' | 'empty',
    typecheckState: TypecheckMethodologyState
  ): string;
  type TypecheckMethodologyState =
    | { kind: 'success-clean-full' }
    | { kind: 'success-with-diagnostics' }
    | { kind: 'success-partial-coverage' }
    | { kind: 'unavailable' }
    | { kind: 'timeout' };
  ```
- **Directive composition order** (R4.8):
  1. Diff directive (R4.1 or R4.2) — first; tells the reviewer what to read.
  2. Existing items 1–8 unchanged.
  3. Item 9 hygiene (existing) unchanged.
  4. **Item 10 typecheck** (new) — R4.4, R4.5 (composed with R4.4 when partial coverage), R4.6, or R4.7 depending on `typecheckState`. Emitted only if not `success-clean-full`.
- **Caller** (`handlePrepare`) computes `diffState` and `typecheckState` from the pre-computed results and passes them in.

### `src/multi-server.ts` (modified)

- Four callsites switch to `resolveRunnerModel(settings, runner)`:
  - L780–791 (adversarial initial): `runner = 'adversarial'`.
  - L948–959 (adversarial retry): `runner = 'adversarial'`. Same value as initial because `loadSettings` returns the cached parse for unchanged files (R3.9).
  - L1730–1742 (task-review initial): `runner = 'taskReview'`.
  - L1774–1786 (task-review retry): `runner = 'taskReview'`.
- `cli` and `cliArgs` continue to read top-level `settings.cli` / `settings.cliArgs` unchanged.

## Data Models

### `AdversarialSettings` (file shape)

```jsonc
{
  "adversarial": { "model": "claude-opus-4-7" },
  "taskReview":  { "model": "claude-haiku-4-5" },
  "features":    { "typecheck": true },
  "model":       "claude-sonnet-4-6",
  "cli":         "claude",
  "cliArgs":     ["--print", "..."]
}
```

All sub-keys are optional. Unknown keys are silently ignored both at the top level (within reason — non-object `adversarial`/`taskReview`/`features` warn) and within runner / `features` blocks (R3.5, R3.12).

### `data.diff` shape

```ts
{
  diff: string;            // unified diff or ""
  diffStats?: { filesChanged: number; linesAdded: number; linesRemoved: number };
  skippedPaths: string[];
  diffTruncated: boolean;
}
```

`diffStats` is omitted when `diff === ""`.

### `data.typecheckResults` shape

`TypecheckResult[]` — see `src/core/typecheck.ts` interface above. Length is always 1 in v1; future multi-config support adds entries without a schema break.

## Error Handling

### Error Scenarios

1. **`git` missing / not a git repo / `git diff` non-zero exit**
   - **Handling:** `computeTaskDiff` catches `execFile` rejection, returns `{ diff: '', stats: undefined, skippedPaths, truncated: false }`. Never throws.
   - **User Impact:** `data.diff === ""`, methodology emits the diff-empty fallback directive (R4.2). Review continues with `filesToReview`.

2. **`tsc` missing / `tsconfig.json` absent or unsupported**
   - **Handling:** `runProjectTypecheck` returns one `{ status: 'unavailable', reason }` entry.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.6 (typecheck-unavailable). Review continues.

3. **`tsc` exceeds 30 s**
   - **Handling:** SIGTERM, 2 s grace, SIGKILL. Result is `{ status: 'timeout' }`.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.7. Review continues with the reviewer told to manually scan for type issues.

4. **`tsc` exits non-zero with no parseable output, OR clean exit with empty `--listFiles`**
   - **Handling:** result is `{ status: 'unavailable', reason: 'no-parseable-output' }`. Prevents the regression where every file is reported as excluded due to an output-capture bug.
   - **User Impact:** methodology emits R4.6.

5. **Diff per-file or total truncation cap exceeded**
   - **Handling:** offending file's hunks replaced with `<diff truncated: <file> exceeded per-file/total cap>`; `diffTruncated: true`.
   - **User Impact:** methodology directive notes truncation; reviewer is instructed to read the full file for the truncated paths.

6. **Malformed `adversarial-settings.json`**
   - **Handling:** offending field is ignored as if absent; warning emitted once per process per file path; settings cache stores the partially-parsed result so re-warns happen only after `(mtime, size)` advances.
   - **User Impact:** runner falls back through R3 precedence (legacy `model` → `undefined`). No crash.

7. **Concurrent editor `git status` holding the index lock**
   - **Handling:** `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` env on both `git diff` invocations.
   - **User Impact:** `git diff` proceeds without waiting on the lock.

8. **Symlinked workspace paths (pnpm) producing false `excluded` entries**
   - **Handling:** R2.4 normalization (`fs.realpathSync.native` + case-fold on case-insensitive volumes) on both sides of the set ops.
   - **User Impact:** coverage matches user expectation; pinned by a fixture test.

## Testing Strategy

### Unit Testing

**Vitest, co-located in `__tests__/`.**

- `src/core/__tests__/path-denylist.test.ts` — exact basename, suffix, prefix, path-segment, case-insensitivity, test-fixture exception (R1.6), binary tagging.
- `src/core/__tests__/task-diff.test.ts` — empty repo, no working-tree changes, basic hunks, denylist filtering, binary-stripping, per-file truncation, total truncation, `git` missing, non-zero exit, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` propagation. Tests use `fs.mkdtemp()` + `git init` per existing test conventions (`hygiene-signals.test.ts:11`).
- `src/core/__tests__/typecheck.test.ts` — clean success, success with in-scope and out-of-scope diagnostics, partial coverage (`exclude` keeps a file out), `'no-tsconfig'`, `'project-references'`, `'wrapper-config'`, `'tsc-not-found'`, `'no-parseable-output'` for both clean-exit-empty-listFiles and non-zero-exit-no-diagnostics, `'feature-disabled'`, timeout (force a 50 ms timeout in test), pnpm-style symlinked path normalization (R2.4), 100-diagnostic cap with in-scope-first ordering.
- `src/core/__tests__/adversarial-settings.test.ts` — the R3.10 precedence matrix: (a) grouped only, (b) legacy only, (c) both with grouped winning, (d) empty string falls back to legacy, (e) `null` treated as absent, (f) unknown sub-keys ignored, (g) malformed top-level tolerated. Plus cache: same `(mtime, size)` returns cached value; advancing `(mtime, size)` re-parses; same mtime + different size re-parses (R3.7 NFS/SMB/WSL2 case); malformed-warn emits once per process and resets when `(mtime, size)` advances. Plus `isTypecheckEnabled`: `false` only when `features.typecheck === false`; everything else returns `true`.
- `src/core/__tests__/hygiene-signals.test.ts` (existing, extended) — denylist-skipped files are not scanned; test-fixture exception lets fixture files through.

### Integration Testing

- `src/tools/__tests__/review-task.test.ts` (existing, extended) — full `handlePrepare` flow with a fixture project: confirms `data.diff`, `data.diffStats`, `data.skippedPaths`, `data.diffTruncated`, `data.typecheckResults` are populated correctly; confirms `Promise.all` shell runs concurrently (assert wall-clock < sum of synthetic delays).
- **Composite-pin tests** (R4.10): 8 scenarios per track stage, each pinning `buildReviewMethodology(...)` byte-equal to a fixture file under `src/tools/__tests__/__fixtures__/methodology/*.txt` after `.trimEnd()` per line and unified `\n`. Axes:
  - **Typecheck axis** (5 fixtures, diff held at present-untruncated): `success-clean-full`, `success-with-diagnostics`, `success-partial-coverage`, `unavailable`, `timeout`.
  - **Diff axis** (3 fixtures, typecheck held at success-clean-full): `diff-empty`, `diff-present-untruncated`, `diff-present-truncated`.
- **Track-A interim pins** (R4.9): committed in Track A's PR (typecheck directives only, no diff directive section). **Track B's PR deletes them** when adding the full-composite pins.

### End-to-End Testing

- **Manual E2E**: invoke `review-task action: prepare` against a small TypeScript fixture repo with uncommitted changes and at least one TS error in scope. Confirm dashboard renders the new fields and the methodology emits the expected directives. Repeat with `features.typecheck: false` to confirm kill switch path.
- **Multi-server settings E2E**: edit `.spec-workflow/adversarial-settings.json` mid-session, trigger an adversarial review and a task review, confirm each runner gets its respective `--model` from the grouped shape; remove the grouped shape and confirm legacy `model` is used; remove all model fields and confirm no `--model` flag is passed.
- No automated E2E harness exists in this repo today; manual E2E remains the convention.
